The Up and Up is a North Carolina-based funk and soul supergroup featuring an all-star lineup of veteran musicians. They blend funk, R&B, jazz, blues, and classic rock. The band is known for its high-energy stage presence, danceable grooves, and soulful original music.The band draws inspiration from funk and soul pioneers like Parliament Funkadelic, The Meters, Curtis Mayfield, and Prince, alongside blues/jam acts like The Allman Brothers Band.

item.title: Max Patch Bald; a Saunter — Mon Sep 28, 9:20 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends Hike a section of the famous Appalachian Trail on top of Max Patch Mountain. This 4,600-foot mountain was cleared and used as pasture in the 1800s. Today, it's a 350-acre tract of open land on a high knob with 360-degree views. On a clear day, you can see from Mt. Mitchell on the east to the Great Smoky Mountains on the south. Before we get there, we will take a side stop at Little Falls Branch Falls We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !! This event is dependent on ‘nice’ weather. **John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. *“We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”*** WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON. I currently have 3 driver(s) (=12ppl) **WE WILL SPEND (up to) an HOUR AT THE ‘TOP’ TO ‘ENJOY’.** Bring ground cloth, snacks & water. **MAX PATCH** details:: Difficulty: Well developed easy trail; constant gradual climb. Length: 2.0 mi total

item.title: Choosing Peace After Loss: Israel/Palestine, Civil Discourse, and the Courage to Listen — Sun Oct 4, 2:00 PM
item.description:
The UNC Asheville Center for Jewish Studies presents Aziz Abu Sarah, co-author of “The Future Is Peace: A Shared Journey Across the Holy Land.” Drawing from his experiences and work in peacebuilding, Abu Sarah will explore nonviolence, dialogue, shared humanity, and the possibility of choosing peace after profound loss. The presentation will be followed by a book signing. This event is free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of Highsmith Student Union. Click here to register for this event.
Accessibility UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu.

item.title: Katherine Min Memorial Reading with Jennifer Sperry Steinorth — Thu Oct 8, 6:00 PM
item.description: Jennifer Sperry Steinorth will visit UNC Asheville for the Katherine Min Memorial Reading. The reading will be held in the Blue Ridge Room of Highsmith Student Union and is free and open to the public. About Jennifer Sperry Steinorth Jennifer Sperry Steinorth’s books include “Boys Behind Glass,” “Her Read: A Graphic Poem,” and “A Wake with Nine Shades.” She is a finalist for the Eric Hoffer Prize, a recipient of the Foreword Reviews Bronze Prize for Poetry, and a recipient of the Fred Whitehead Award from the Texas Institute of Letters. A poet, educator, interdisciplinary artist & licensed builder, she has received grants from Yale, Vermont Studio Center, the Sewanee Writers Conference, and the Community of Writers & the Institute for Research on Women & Gender at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, where she is a lecturer in the English Department. item.title: Lea and Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp — Fri Oct 9, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Gaelynn Lea and Kalyn Rose Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp will visit UNC Asheville for an afternoon talk and evening performance. At 3 p.m., Lea and Heffernan will discuss disability culture, access, and activism, sharing their experiences as artists and advocates working to make the arts more inclusive. At 6 p.m., Wheelchair Sports Camp will take the stage for a free performance. Lea, winner of NPR Music’s Tiny Desk Contest, is an accomplished violinist, songwriter, composer, and disability advocate who has performed around the world and composed the score for Macbeth on Broadway. Wheelchair Sports Camp, led by wheelchair-using rapper Kalyn Rose Heffernan, blends hip-hop, humor, and high-energy performance. The Denver-based band has expanded its work beyond music into performance art, museums, theater, film, and activism. Both events are free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of the Highsmith Student Union.
Accessibility UNC Ashe

item.title: Code with Asheville Open Project / Co-Work Day — Sat Oct 10, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Tech Events ## Details
Join us for our monthly project/co-working day! Bring your own project for co-working or jump in on an existing project. We can use all different kinds of support, from emailing to data entry to coding.
**Location:** Hi Wire Brewing - Biltmore Village / Guajiro Cuban food truck 2A Huntsman Pl, Asheville, NC 28803
**What to expect:** (Feel free to drop in when you can and leave when you need to.)
* *11am*: Arrival and introductions. Say hi and catch up with your Code with Asheville crew. * *11:15-11:30am*: Folks chat through what they hope to accomplish for the day, ask for help, and divide into small groups for certain projects. This is a great place to get plugged in if you're looking for a project to work on. * *11:30am*: We get to work! Some of us stay in the main meeting chat room while we work, others go heads offline. * 1-2*pm*: Wrap up our work for that day until next time
Source: Asheville Tech Events
